title: A private nested class as a hidden component

blocks.text: A class may declare **nested classes** as components of its own. The page asks you to weigh their pros and cons. Used well, a nested class is a private building block nobody outside can see or depend on. Declared `static`, its objects do not each carry a hidden reference to an outer object.
Write `LinkedStack<T>`, a stack built from linked nodes:

items: `push(T value)`, `pop()` (removes and returns the top value), `peek()` (returns the top value without removing it), `size()` and `isEmpty()`;
`pop()` and `peek()` on an empty stack throw `java.util.NoSuchElementException`;
the node type is **one** nested class of `LinkedStack`, `private` and `static`, holding a value and the next node. No other nested class is declared.

blocks.text:
s.push(1); s.push(2); s.push(3)
s.pop()   -> 3
s.peek()  -> 2
s.size()  -> 2
new LinkedStack<String>().pop() -> NoSuchElementException

cases.says: Values come back from pop in the reverse of the order they were pushed, and size follows.
pop and peek on an empty stack throw NoSuchElementException.
The stack declares exactly one nested class, and it is private and static.

concepts: A private static nested class is a hidden component of its outer class, and its objects carry no reference to an outer object.
